reviewer: Claude Sonnet genetic-perturbation-response evidence-research worker, independently reviewed by Codex
scope: Bounded additive genetic-perturbation-response evidence intake (B334/BL334, rewire-benchmarks #25; programme rewire-benchmark-data #3; article plan rewire.it #334). Adds PertEval-scFM (Wenteler et al., ICML 2025, PMLR v267 pp.66633-66677), Table 1, Norman single-gene section, 2,000 HVGs, AUSPC column, three configurations: GEARS (trained from scratch, no pretrained weights; 0.815 ± 0.039), MLP baseline (input Xc concatenated with perturbed-gene co-expression features, Eq. 3; 4.484 ± 0.299), Mean baseline (predicted effect = mean expression of all cells in the same context minus the cell's own expression, per the source's own text, population not restricted to controls or training cells in that text; 4.612 ± 0.317), all x10^-2 as printed. Scores the perturbation-effect delta=P-Xc (Eq. 5, described by the source as a 'log fold change perturbation effect'), not raw post-perturbation expression, and a different metric construction from GEARS Supplementary Table 6's own Pearson-delta-expression metric. AUSPC's printed uncertainty is the source's own propagated standard error (Appendix F.2 propagation formula; main-text Figure 2 caption wording), attributed to triplicate experiments per model (Appendix I, Figure I1 caption, which separately states '8 train-test splits' against Table 1's seven S-columns -- preserved as printed, not resolved). Experimental lane: 12 records (1 source, 1 dataset subset, 1 protocol, 3 configurations, 3 evaluations, 3 results); clinical and research lanes are empty scaffolding only. One new proxy mapping on use-case-genetic-perturbation-response (use-case-map-perteval-scfm-norman-single-auspc). This is a second, independent, full-text-verified GEARS evaluation distinct from the existing GEARS Supplementary Table 6 catalogue entries (different gene universe, split mechanism and metric construction); the eight existing Table 6 results and two mappings remain byte-identical. Reconciled to the focused execution gap opened at rewire-benchmarks #29 (frozen Norman control panel, metric-sensitivity check, separately registered context-transfer protocol), which this source-transcription intake does not close.
limitations: Automated source review only (Claude local extraction, independently reviewed by Codex against the primary PDF, the pinned GitHub code at commit ce48c8b998901c8f8b6275114caac3a4d8543c0b, and the PMLR general publication agreement); not qualified human scientific review or independent experimental replication.

Proxy relevance only: expression-change-prediction endpoint, the same proxy class as the existing Table 6 mappings; does not establish prospective experiment-selection hit rate (case 6, use-case-phenotype-perturbation-selection, is the separate endpoint for that question).

Per-sparsification-split (S0.1-S0.7) scored perturbation counts are not printed by the source and are not computed or inferred here; the source's own eligible raw single-gene perturbation count (105, Appendix A.1) is the compiled dataset total, not a per-split scored count.

The source's own Table 1 double-gene section contains an internal printed arithmetic inconsistency (GEARS AUSPC 0.808, Mean-baseline AUSPC 4.255, printed Delta 4.254, where 4.255-0.808=3.447) and its Table 2 (Replogle RPE1, not part of this intake) contains a running-text-vs-table-row labeling conflict; neither is resolved by this pass.

The Mean baseline's input population ('all cells in the same context') is not fully specified by the paper's Section 2.2 text (control vs. all cells; training vs. all splits is not stated there). A separately dated, independently pinned code observation (commit ce48c8b998901c8f8b6275114caac3a4d8543c0b, MeanExpression.forward) computes a batch mean of the first half of whatever input is passed at call time; this is recorded as a distinct, dated fact, not merged with the paper's definition, and the code commit's correspondence to the published run is unverified.

GEARS in this intake is an independent from-scratch training run by PertEval-scFM's authors (official implementation, train-test splits modified to align with SPECTRA, other parameters at default values, no pretrained weights), not the original GEARS authors' own Table 6 checkpoint/run.

Input populations differ across the three intaken configurations (GEARS's graph-based architecture; the MLP baseline's Xc-plus-co-expression features; the Mean baseline's non-learned context mean) and are not an identical input budget.

This protocol concerns generalisation to unseen perturbations under SPECTRA's distribution-shift splits; it does not test or establish forecasting for unseen cells, donors, or cell-line/context transfer.

use-case-genetic-perturbation-response remains an incomplete, open evidence-collection case. A confirmed, directly relevant 27-method/29-dataset benchmark (scPerturBench, Wei et al., Nat. Methods) remains genuinely paywalled and unread. This intake does not close the focused execution gap tracked at rewire-benchmarks #29.
